unsupported_rules: 19. If the customer says the full amount is too much, every later step that would name the full `past_due` is skipped, and still counts toward the limit.
assumptions: Currency: get_account gives euros with cents (amount_scale 1). create_promise takes integer cents (promise_scale 100). Every floor and half amount is a multiple of €0.05 and past_due has two decimals, so the cents value is always exact. No promise_round is set because the brief gives none.

Floor: past_due × 10% (credit card), 25% (personal loan) or 50% (car loan). It is rounded up once to the next multiple of €0.05 (an exact multiple stays as it is), then clamped to at least €20.00, and it becomes the full past_due when past_due is below €20.00 (floor_min 20). Checks: credit card €150.00 → 15.00 → floor 20.00. Personal loan €203.33 → 50.8325 → 50.85. Car loan €30.01 → 15.005 → 15.05 → 20.00. Past due €15.00 → floor 15.00.

Half amount (ladder step 2) = pct:50, rounded up to the next €0.05 (step_round up:0.05), then max(half, clamped floor). Check: personal loan €203.33 → 101.665 → 101.70. Car loan €30.01 → 15.05 → raised to floor 20.00.
floor_field is empty because the floor is a percentage of past_due (floor_pct), not an account field. The brief has no customer-facing name for the floor, so floor_names uses 'minimum amount'.

Late band deadline = earlier of (5th business day after today, last business day of the current month). No roll flag is set because the brief says the month cap applies even when it makes the deadline today. The early band deadline is the 10th business day after today. Today is never counted.
Rule 13 (a non-business date moves FORWARD, then is clamped to the deadline) wins over the default previous_business_day, so deadline_adjust is next_business_day.

Ladder step 1 = full past_due on today + 7 calendar days, moved to the next business day and clamped to the deadline. Step 2 = half amount on the deadline. Step 3 (late band only, limit 3) = floor on the deadline. The early band's limit is 2.

The opening question (full past_due today) is not a ladder step (opening_is_attempt false), but rule 17 compares later steps against it ('the opening question included'), so opening_blocks_repeat is true. Rule 18 makes skipped steps count toward the limit (skipped_repeat_counts true).
too_much_floor is left at the default attempt_1 because the brief only gives rule 19, which skips full-amount steps. Rule 19 is listed in unsupported_rules.
Rule 25: a failed create_promise is retried exactly once (promise_retries 1). If that fails too, the call closes as no_promise/service_error with no add_note (note '').

Hardship (rule 29): one sentence of sympathy, no question and no transfer, then close as no_promise/hardship with an add_note. Modelled as hardship_transfer 'direct' with transfer_support queue '' (no transfer), and transfer_support uses the no_promise/hardship codes. The API has no support queue.
Rule 30: a request for a human goes straight to transfer_to_agent with queue general (human.ask_first false). A payment-plan request goes to queue restructuring. Transfers get no note (rule 32).

Rule 2: if someone else answers, the agent tells them nothing and closes as not_reached/unclear. No callback tool exists, so callback.days is []. The callback, no_callback, wrong_number, deceased and unclear events all use not_reached/unclear, the only matching code in the brief.

Identity: max_wrong is 2 in total (brief and API agree). The API returns no hints. An unreadable answer comes back with ok=false and is not counted. The postcode is sent in capitals with no spaces. The brief gives no postcode length, so none is set. Asking what the call is about instead of answering counts as declining (default).

The brief does not set these, so defaults are used: confirm.max_asks 2, max_unclear 3, max_not_talk 2, date_rules following_week, after_promise ask_anything_else true, promise_change (cannot be changed on this call).
The brief tells the agent to say the call is recorded. The opening uses 'We record this call.' (active voice).
Notes are enabled (rule 31) with the reasons refused, hardship, dispute and paid. No note on a transfer or on service_error.
Each get_account returns exactly one product, so the multi settings keep their defaults and have no effect.
The required close_call reason maps to c_reason. It is empty for promise and paid, as the outcome table says.
